methods: duration-proportional row replication at a temporal resolution
density lookup along the sampled trajectory (sample_density with times)
cases.estimand: The fixation position in force at each requested time, the rows implied by each fixation's duration at a stated temporal resolution, and the template-density value at the sampled positions. Every output is a deterministic function of its inputs; eyesim draws nothing at random here.
conventions: a time before the first onset is NA on both paths
after the last onset both paths hold the last fixation
neither path consults duration, so a gap between fixations keeps the preceding position
equal onsets resolve to the later row on both paths
rep_fixations repeats each row floor(duration * resolution) times with a floating-point tolerance, never fewer than once
sample_density returns NA wherever the sampled trajectory is NA
requested and realized cardinality both retained
cases.independent_case: A two-fixation path queried before its first onset, at and between onsets, after the last onset and after the last fixation ends separates the fast and slow endpoint policies from a duration-aware lookup; a duration of 0.29 at resolution 100, 29 steps in exact arithmetic, exposes the floating-point truncation to 28 rows; a duplicated onset exposes the averaging.
cases.divergence: Ordered and singleton onset trajectories agree with both pinned paths under HoldLastOnset, as do density-time composition and the 29-row replication at 0.29 seconds and 100 Hz. Native duplicate onsets are refused where the pinned paths take the later row, and empty support is explicit missing data where R's constructor fails. OnsetRange remains a named native alternative.

cases.estimand: A seeded finite sample of eligible controls with the realized candidate set and denominator retained.
conventions: R seed and RNGkind recorded for optimized density and generic fixation facades
native excludes all true-match copies before selection
positive native cap; zero explicitly rejected
cases.independent_case: A cap of one over the two eligible controls detects priority, target-exclusion and denominator errors.
cases.divergence: Pinned R removes every true-match copy and counts each distinct template once before drawing, so its realized count is min(cap,eligible templates). Native relations exclude all same-match candidates before keyed BottomK and produce min(cap,eligible); pairing against a one-row-per-template table reproduces every exhaustive reference row, while pairing against source occurrences keeps their multiplicity by construction. Zero cap is a native typed error versus R no-control analysis. R optimized/generic cap-one draws differ; no PRNG identity is claimed. Native missing/ambiguous keys remain values. template_sample is deterministic density lookup, measured with the shared trajectory.
